pr_title: Deprecate empty collection for retrying all methods
git_commit_log:
Deprecate empty collection for retrying all methods (#5223)
Drop request body framing state on 303 redirects (#5161)

* Drop request body framing state on 303 redirects

A 303 makes urllib3 switch the method to GET and discard the request
body per RFC 9110, Section 15.4.4, but the state describing that body
survived the switch.

The redirected request kept its chunked framing, so a bodyless GET went
out carrying "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" and an empty chunked body. It
also kept body_pos, so a file-like body made the redirect fail with
"ValueError: body_pos must be of type integer, instead it was
<class 'int'>" while trying to rewind a body that no longer existed.

Reset chunked and body_pos alongside the body in both
HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen() and PoolManager.urlopen(), and discard
Transfer-Encoding in HTTPHeaderDict._prepare_for_method_change() to
cover bodies framed by an explicit header rather than the chunked
keyword.

test_redirect_with_failed_tell used /redirect, which defaults to 303, so
it asserted UnrewindableBodyError for a body that never needed rewinding.
Point it at status=307, which preserves the body and genuinely requires a
rewind, matching how test_redirect_put_file already selects 307 for
body-preserving coverage. The 303 case is now covered explicitly by
test_303_redirect_with_failed_tell.

* Test 303 redirect body framing against the dummy server

Replace the socket-level tests with assertions on the headers echoed back
by the dummy server, next to the existing 303 tests, and shorten the
changelog entry.

* Trigger CI after flaky job timeout

* Close the connection in the 303 body framing tests

The chunked request body is never read by the server, since nothing
routes it to a form parser, so reusing the connection let the leftover
body desynchronize the redirected GET and hang the client. Ask for the
connection to be closed instead.

* Let the server read the body in the 303 framing tests

The chunked body is only read when it is announced as a form. Left
unread, it desynchronized the redirected request on the reused
connection and hung the client until the job timed out.

Name the headers being sent apart from the ones echoed back, since the
two are different types.

* Drain the request body in dummyserver's redirect handler

/redirect read the body through `request.values`, which only parses it
for form content types. A request carrying any other kind of body got
its redirect while the body was still sitting in the socket, and the
leftover bytes then desynchronized the next request on the reused
connection.

Read the body unconditionally, keeping form parsing for the handlers and
tests that depend on it. The 303 framing tests no longer have to disguise
their bodies as forms to avoid hanging.
